claims.claim_ar: افتتاح آية بـ«ذَلِكَ» كأداة إشاريّة للتنظير والتوكيد، أسلوب حكيم يوجّه الانتباه إلى حكم شامل (الكتاب) قبل بيان صفاته.
claims.claim_en: The opening demonstrative 'dhālika' functions as a pointing device that frames and emphasizes the statement — a rhetorical, wise stylistic move that directs attention to a general judgment (the Book) before specifying its qualities.
claims.needs_review_reason: Inference based on general rhetorical function of demonstratives; provided chunks contain 'وَكَذلِكَ' but do not explicitly analyse the demonstrative 'ذَلِكَ' in relation to this specific ayah.

claims.claim_ar: التضاد البلاغي بين تعريف «الْكِتَابُ» وتنكير «هُدًى» يبرز كون الكتاب معرفاً شاملاً بينما تبتدع النكرة صفةً خاصّة (الهدى) موجهة لفئة معينة (المتقين).
claims.claim_en: A rhetorical contrast of definiteness: the definite 'al-kitāb' (the Book) vs. the indefinite 'hudā' (a guidance) highlights the Book's general, established status while presenting guidance as a particular, benefit aimed at a specific group (the God‑conscious).
claims.needs_review_reason: The source chunk contains the word-form 'الْكِتابِ' but does not explicitly discuss this specific definite/indefinite contrast for the ayah; the claim is an informed inference that should be checked against specialized balāgha commentary.

warnings: Provided source chunks are primarily iʻrāb notes and do not contain explicit balāgha (rhetoric) commentary on Sura 2:2; many standard balagha observations (e.g., on «لا ريبَ فيه» or on concision/inimitability) are not present in the chunks.

Some claims are inferred from word-forms found in the chunks (e.g., 'مِنَ الْكِتابِ', 'وَكَذلِكَ') rather than supported by explicit rhetorical analysis in those chunks — please review classical balagha/tafsir-balāgha sources (al-Jurjānī, al-Sakkākī, al-Bāqillānī, al-Suyūṭī, tafsīr balāgha) for confirmation and fuller evidence.
